Theme

School & learning

subject noun

at school or university

also school subject, studies

classical

Cic. Cael. 72: dēdita disciplīnīs (Lewis & Short)
Traupman 32, 387
M-O s.v. teach (a subject)

disciplīna, disciplīnae f.

noun, first declension

a subject, a branch of learning

Lewis & Short: instruction, learning, science. To teach a subject, disciplīnam trādere (Morgan–Owens).

Other words

  • ars, artis f. — an art, a body of knowledge with its rules

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · Cic. Cael. 72: iīsque artibus, quibus īnstruimur (Lewis & Short)

  • studia, studiōrum n. pl. — studies, what one studies

    noun, second declension, plural · also used · classical · Cic. Q. fr. 3.9.2: litterae mē et studia nostra … dēlectant; Traupman 31

Examples

  • cujus prīma aetās dēdita disciplīnīs fuit iīsque artibus, quibus īnstruimur ad hunc ūsum forēnsem

    whose early years were given to study, and to the subjects that train us for this work in the courtsCic. Cael. 72

  • Quae disciplīna tibi maximē placet?

    Which subject do you like best?composed

See also subject, lesson, school, student.

SourcesLewis & Short: disciplina · Lewis & Short: ars · Lewis & Short: studium
